_comment: Genestealer Cults army rule citations (10e). Two entries cover the Cult Ambush army rule: simulator.cult_ambush handles the turn-1 redeploy approximation (army-wide Deep Strike at the top of Round 1); simulator.cult_ambush_resurgence handles the Resurgence-point unit revival approximation at round end. Both are APPROXIMATIONS — the verbatim rule uses Cult Ambush markers, Strategic Reserves, and a per-unit Resurgence-point table the simulator cannot reproduce in full.

simulator.cult_ambush.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is Genestealer Cults, you start the battle with a number of Resurgence points, depending on the battle size, as shown below. Incursion: 6 Resurgence points. Strike Force: 10 Resurgence points. Onslaught: 14 Resurgence points. Each time a unit from your army is destroyed, if every model in that unit has this ability you can spend the relevant number of Resurgence points shown below based on that unit's Starting Strength. If you do: Add a new unit to your army identical to your destroyed unit, in Cult Ambush, at its Starting Strength, with all of its wounds remaining and any [ONE SHOT] weapons those models are equipped with considered as not having been shot. Place one Cult Ambush marker (see below) anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9" horizontally away from all enemy units (if this is not possible, no marker is placed). UNITS IN CULT AMBUSH: Cult Ambush is a type of Strategic Reserves. Units in Cult Ambush cannot be targeted with the Rapid Ingress Stratagem, but can be set up on the battlefield using a Cult Ambush marker as described below, or by following the rules for Strategic Reserves in a subsequent turn.
simulator.cult_ambush.trigger: start of battle (initial Resurgence allocation); each time a GSC unit is destroyed (revival option)
simulator.cult_ambush.effect: (APPROXIMATION) at the start of Round 1, every GSC unit is routed to the simulator's reserves bucket at deployment time instead of placed on the standard deployment line, and arrives via the existing Deep Strike landing-point picker (> 9" from every enemy model, A UnitDeepStrike event per landing). The marker-placement / opponent-disruption / Reinforcements step half of the rule is NOT modelled here — see simulator.cult_ambush_resurgence for the revival half.

simulator.cult_ambush_resurgence.rule_name: Cult Ambush (Resurgence points / unit revival half)
simulator.cult_ambush_resurgence.quoted_text: Each time a unit from your army is destroyed, if every model in that unit has this ability you can spend the relevant number of Resurgence points shown below based on that unit's Starting Strength. If you do: Add a new unit to your army identical to your destroyed unit, in Cult Ambush, at its Starting Strength, with all of its wounds remaining and any [ONE SHOT] weapons those models are equipped with considered as not having been shot.
simulator.cult_ambush_resurgence.trigger: end of any round; GSC army has Resurgence points remaining AND at least one destroyed CULT INFANTRY unit
simulator.cult_ambush_resurgence.effect: (APPROXIMATION) at end of round, one dead INFANTRY unit (excluding CHARACTERs) is restored to full Starting Strength and placed > 9" from every alive enemy via the Deep Strike landing-point fallback, costing a flat 3 Resurgence points per revival (median of the codex per-Starting-Strength table: 2–8 points). The unit is flagged in _fresh_arrivals so it skips its movement sub-phase the following round, mirroring an ambush drop. The codex's Cult Ambush marker placement, opponent move-too-close marker removal, and the per-unit Resurgence cost table are NOT modelled — the proxy collapses the entire mechanic to one revival per round at a flat cost. Initial Resurgence pool = 10 (Strike Force default).
